transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-18 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Iridium - Head of ML), Carlos Ruiz (Iridium - Platform Eng), Jonah Becker (Iridium CPO)
Recorded at: 2026-12-18T16:00:00Z

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off, um, I know Jonah had to jump on for the intro, appreciate it, uh Aisha and Carlos thanks for your time.
[00:08] Jonah: yeah hi all short intro from me - we're looking to validate a vendor for a pilot to power our customer support synthesis and insights feature. Key for us is predictable cost and sub-300ms p95 for single-turn summarization where possible.
[00:20] Aisha: yep, and to add - our current in-house system is at about 150ms average but p95 spikes to 800ms under load, and cost is unpredictable. We're here to understand Redwood's unit economics and tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated.
[00:35] Liam: great, thanks. quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, cost model walkthrough, and next steps. we'll go through an initial per-token estimate with knobs like batching and KV caching.
[00:46] Maya: quick qualification q - expected peak QPS during pilot?
[00:50] Aisha: for pilot we expect 20 sustained QPS, burst to 50 for short periods, average tokens per request about 180 (input+output) - some requests are shorter, some longer.
[01:05] Carlos: we have a monthly budget cap of $20k for the pilot - that's a hard constraint.
[01:12] Liam: ok noted. I'll outline a few costing scenarios: baseline hosted with no caching, dedicated with batching tuned, and dedicated + KV/prefix caching.

[01:30] Liam: rough math first - at 20 QPS that's ~1.7M requests/day, sorry that's wrong - uh, that's if 20 qps sustained 24/7, but pilot will be limited to business hours. Let's use realistic window: 12 hours/day, so about ~864k requests/day. with 180 tokens per request that's ~155M tokens/day. monthly that's... math, around 4.6B tokens/month. (somewhat approximate).
[01:58] Aisha: wow that seems high, I think our live pilot footprint will be lower; our internal estimate was more like 600k requests/month. I must clarify - the 20 QPS was peak. average qps is likely 2-3.
[02:12] Maya: good callout - important to pin the traffic profile. Aisha can you share a 7-day sample?
[02:18] Aisha: yes I'll send logs, will anonymize.

[02:30] Liam: okay, let's model two workloads: conservative (average 3 QPS, 12 business hrs) and aggressive (20 QPS peak bursts). For conservative: 3 QPS over 12 hours => ~129.6k requests/day => ~23M tokens/day => ~690M tokens/month. For aggressive bursty it's the earlier 4.6B/month number.
[02:58] Liam: per-token costs depend on model and execution; a typical hosted large model profile here for generation might be approx $X per 1M tokens for hosted, and on Dedicated unit costs drop because of amortized GPU. For POC scoping we'll provide ranges: hosted: $10-40 per 1M tokens depending on model size and latency tier; dedicated: $3-15 per 1M tokens depending on utilization and batching.
[03:24] Carlos: those ranges are wide - can you walk through assumptions?
[03:28] Liam: yes - hosted includes infrastructure, autoscaling, and multi-tenant overhead. Dedicated assumes reserved GPU capacity where we can get better per-token with high utilization and aggressive batching. Key knobs: batch size, max latency SLO allowed, and prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts.

[03:45] Maya: quick example calculation: conservative workload 690M tokens/month * hosted $20/1M => $13.8k/month. Dedicated at $6/1M => $4.14k/month. With caching we might reduce token volume by 30-40% for repeated prompts which further reduces cost.
[04:05] Aisha: caching sounds promising - our use case has a lot of repeated system prompts and semi-structured responses so caching could be effective. How invasive is implementation?
[04:15] Liam: KV/prefix caching is mostly runtime-level; you can use it without modifying your app significantly. We do need to identify reusable prefixes and provide a small integration to store key IDs. We'll show example code.

[04:30] [small crosstalk]
[04:35] Jonah: what about latency tradeoffs when batching? we need p95 < 300ms ideally.
[04:40] Liam: batching improves throughput and cost per token but increases tail latency. For p95 < 300ms we have two levers: limit batch size and/or use a lower-latency model variant (quantized or smaller model) for latency-sensitive routes. Also fast-path on dedicated GPUs with optimized kernels helps. We typically recommend a hybrid: latency-critical endpoints use small batch (or no batching) on dedicated nodes; background/async work can use larger batching.

[05:05] Maya: can you both confirm expected p95 with different configurations? rough numbers are fine.
[05:10] Liam: sure - on a mid-sized A100-equivalent dedicated pool with optimized kernels:
- no batching, small model variant: p95 ~140-220ms
- batching of up to 4: p95 ~180-350ms (depends on sequence length)
- batching up to 8: p95 likely >350ms for long sequences
These are approximate and we'll validate with the benchmark.

[05:42] Carlos: our SLO is strict on p95 at 300ms; if batching to 4 sometimes crosses 300ms that's risky. Do you support route-level policies?
[05:50] Maya: yes - Redwood supports routing by policy: you can pin critical endpoints to low-latency capacity or a small-model variant and let other traffic go to a higher-throughput pool.

[06:05] Aisha: what about quality tradeoff when using smaller models or quantized ones - we need to keep extraction accuracy above 94% for our tests.
[06:12] Liam: that's a quality constraint - we'll run evals on your prompt set as part of the benchmark. If small model drops under 94% we'll fallback to a larger variant for that route. Also quantization sometimes causes small regressions; we can test quantized variants and include quality delta in the cost model.

[06:30] Jonah: can you summarize pilot success criteria so we align?
[06:34] Maya: sure, draft success criteria: 1) End-to-end p95 latency for critical route <= 300ms for 95% of requests during business hours; 2) Unit cost for the pilot does not exceed $20k/month under conservative traffic profile; 3) Quality (extraction/summary accuracy) >= 94% on your eval prompt set; 4) Security checklist: SOC2 + SSO integration verified.
[06:58] Aisha: that matches our expectations; we'll add compliance items.

[07:06] Liam: benchmark plan: provision a dedicated 2-GPU pool (A100-equivalent), run a 48-hour synthetic run using your 5k prompts scaled to target QPS profile, and collect p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, and token counts. We'll run three configs:
- config A: no batching, low-latency model
- config B: batch size 4, standard model
- config C: batch size 8 + KV caching enabled for repeated prefixes
We'll also run quality evals against your gold outputs.

[07:45] Carlos: for the benchmark, can you emit raw logs and a CSV for our perf team? we want GPU metrics and token breakdown by request.
[07:52] Liam: yes we'll share a benchmark report and a CSV. we'll point to a shared folder link - we'll use: https://redwood.prod/poc/iridium-benchmark (placeholder link).

[08:05] Maya: cost model detail: we'll send a spreadsheet with columns for tokens/month, per-1M-token cost, infra amortization, network egress, and bench-derived multipliers. We'll include sensitivity analysis for utilization (50%, 75%, 95%) since dedicated per-token drops significantly as utilization rises.

[08:25] Aisha: can you give a quick example with our conservative estimate? let's assume conservative 690M tokens/month - what should we expect?
[08:30] Liam: quick example: at dedicated $6/1M => 690 * $6 = $4,140 / month. Add infra overhead (reserved pool cost) say $2k/month amortized for the pool during pilot => $6,140. With caching reducing tokens 30% => tokens -> 483M => cost -> $2,898 + infra = ~$4,898. All still under $20k. Hosted with $20/1M => 690*$20 = $13,800/month, plus possible autoscale bumps.

[08:58] Jonah: okay that gives us headroom; but again pilot budget is a hard constraint we won't exceed.

[09:04] Aisha: any compliance blockers for Dedicated or Private deployment? we have to keep logs for 12 months and ensure KMS integration.
[09:11] Liam: Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs retention. For Private (VPC) we can provide on-prem options; Dedicated also supports customer-managed keys for encrypting payloads at rest. We'll share the SOC2 and KMS docs.

[09:30] Maya: action item recap: I'll send the cost spreadsheet and sample assumptions; Liam will provision the benchmark; Aisha will provide prompt samples and traffic shape. Carlos will send security checklist items. We'll meet on Jan 5 to review results.

[09:45] Aisha: one small question - if we run the benchmark and utilization is low, can we burst to hosted to save cost?
[09:52] Liam: yes - Redwood supports smart routing and fallback; you can route overflow to hosted API or a lower-priority queue. That can help keep SLOs up while controlling cost - though mixing hosted/dedicated increases complexity and there are cross-region egress costs to consider. We'll model that in the spreadsheet.

[10:10] Jonah: ok last thing - please include a clear per-request example in the spreadsheet showing tokens in/out, batch effect, and final per-request cost. That's most helpful for exec sign-off.

[10:22] Maya: will do.

[10:25] [wrap-up]
[10:28] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with deliverables.
